HOW TO TEST — and why we cannot give you credentials.

Habeas never receives, stores or transmits any password. It works INSIDE the session the user has
already opened themselves, in their own browser. There is therefore no test account we can hand over:
there is no Habeas account, and handing over a real service account would defeat the design.

To evaluate it, use your own account at any supported service. The full catalogue is public at
https://habeas.dev/sources.html — the internationally available ones are easiest for a reviewer:
PayPal, Amazon, AliExpress, Revolut, Trade Republic.

STEPS
1. Install and open the extension. It opens its Archive; no sign-up, no account, no onboarding.
2. Settings > Sources: enable one source for a service you already use (e.g. PayPal or Amazon).
3. Open that service in a tab and sign in yourself, as you normally would, MFA included.
4. Back in Habeas, press Refresh on that source. It lists your own documents and shows them locally.
5. Optionally pick a destination (a plain download is the simplest) and save one document.

WITHOUT any such account you can still verify: the UI, the settings, the source catalogue, the
permission usage and the fact that nothing is transmitted anywhere — the network panel stays silent
until you explicitly act.

NOTES FOR REVIEW
- No remote code. Source definitions are declarative JSON data interpreted by code inside the package;
  they are never evaluated. There is no eval() and no externally referenced script (MV3 compliant).
- No telemetry, no analytics, no developer server. Data goes only to the destination the user picks.
- Broad host access (https://*/*) is OPTIONAL and never granted at install: it is requested at runtime,
  one origin at a time, with the user's click, only when they add a source for a site not built in.
- Open source, AGPL-3.0: https://github.com/habeas-dev/habeas
- Privacy policy: https://habeas.dev/privacy.html
